item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert changes at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

From first glance, you'd think that having these maggots around would be handy, since there is no shortage of cadavers produced by the foundation, and you can use them to regenerate living tissue that can be used in experiments with objects that function via living tissue, like SCP-1361. But then you get to the testing log, and you learn why exactly this is a bad idea. To capitalize on this mind set, I am proposing the following edit:

Changing the following:

Addendum: Testing of SCP-726 has been discontinued following Dr. ██████'s recent findings. The samples at Site-17 should be closely monitored for any inconsistent behavior or abnormal growth.

To this:

Addendum: Testing of SCP-726 has been discontinued following Dr. ██████'s recent findings. Requests to use tissue generated by SCP-726 for experimentation with SCP-1361 and similar anomalies have subsequently been denied. The samples at Site-17 should be closely monitored for any inconsistent behavior or abnormal growth.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like it. It certainly is original and I like what the author did with that concept, although I believe a few rewrites could be done, especially when it comes to tone. For example, several of the notes from the generation experiments feel uncharacteristically… lolfoundation-y, for lack of a better word.

And I don't mind it in small doses, but I feel there's a bit too much and it's a bit too inconsistent with the rest of the article.

I'd keep just a couple of the funniest ones, like the one where a burger from a fast-food restaurant lead to the reconstitution of several rats, which I found genuinely hilarious.

On a different note, I feel some details aren't necessary or could be described better, like the worms multiplying "through unknown means" (how is it unknown if the foundation was monitoring it? If it's irrelevant, I think the best thing to do is to just not bring up that it's unknown) or the worms acting like reverse footage of worm activity, which I understand is pretty cool when you picture it but I feel is worded very awkwardly.

Still, good concept, well executed, upvoted.

item.content:encoded:
It occurs to me…

anything that consumes any animal tissue generated by 726, becomes infected with 726.

Can we actually destroy this stuff? If we incinerate it, and then use the ashes in topsoil, and plants grow from that topsoil, will anything that eats one of those plants become contaminated? Or is it safe once we destroy every last cell, rupturing every membrane and organelle and protein and polypeptide, and reducing it to simple organic compounds?

because otherwise we could be looking at a runaway replicator scenario.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That was the whole idea. This could maybe get away with existing unnoticed because it just looks like a mental condition, but the people are really insects in bodies brought back to life by maggots.

I intended there to be horror in the strangeness of it all. I didn't intend "grossness" or "squick," since I don't find maggots (or any natural organism) to be gross whatsoever. In fact, they're some of my favorite animals…I think they're just plain cool and fascinating, any "gross out" factor to this is purely the reader's creation.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Some other things flies do that reconstructs would imitate, which I left out of the SCP to preserve space and maintain a moderately more serious tone:

-Fail to comprehend transparent surfaces or learn that they cannot go through them, trapping themselves in prolonged loops of bumping into glass doors, windows and screens until they accidentally bump their way to an opaque surface. Only then does their mind say "oh, okay, let's try a different direction now." Sometimes, of course, this leads right back into the glass.

-Thoroughly feel edible-smelling surfaces with their feet (and hands, in human reconstructs) as this is where a fly's taste buds are.

-Repetitively circle around the most prominent, darkest object in a room as a navigational landmark. This is why flies seem to orient around you even if you don't smell like food. Other times they might pick out a ceiling fan or furniture.

-Frequently wipe themselves all over with their limbs to "groom" themselves, especially wiping off their face and eyes of any contaminants. Flies remain pretty filthy since they are after all just smearing gunk around until it's too thin to annoy them.

-Bask in warm, sunlit places for extended periods like a cat.

-Drink the juices generated by their own maggots feeding and defecating in carrion.

-Lick up urine for the nitrates. Butterflies also do this, incidentally, as well as from feces.

-Follow the scent of methane and congregate around cattle or other large animals to feed on whatever comes out of them, or go in for the source and lick the residual waste still clinging to them. Enjoy that one.
